court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Virudhunagar, C.C.No.104 of 2009

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: J.Gnanakumar, husband; V.P.Rajan, Rita Ernest, Sivamayam, Gnanamani Susila, sisters and brother-in-laws of J.Gnanakumar (A1); Muthulakshmi, second wife of J.Gnanakumar

facts_of_case: The petitioners filed criminal original petitions seeking to quash the entire criminal proceedings in C.C.No.104 of 2009, which was filed by the respondent against the petitioners.

legal_principles.principle: A court must apply its judicial mind while taking a complaint on file.
legal_principles.held: The learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Virudhunagar, without applying his judicial mind, had wrongly interpreted the provisions and taken the complaint on his file.

legal_principles.principle: A court cannot take cognizance of an offence punishable under section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, except upon a police report or a complaint made by the person aggrieved.
legal_principles.held: No Court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860), except upon a police report of facts which constitute such offence or upon a complaint made by the person aggrieved by the offence or by her father, mother, brother, sister or by her father's or mother's brother or sister or, with the leave of the Court, by any other person related to her by blood, marriage or adoption.

outcome.final_order: The court granted the relief sought and quashed the criminal proceedings.
